SURFER QUANTLIVE-RECORD GUIDE

How to read returns, equity and drawdown in a trading record

A growth curve is a starting point. Time periods, cash flows and equity data determine meaningful comparisons.

Research guide5 min readPublished by Surfer Quant
01

Identify the period and account type

Live, demo and backtested results should be separated. Cumulative returns need start and end dates. A snapshot represents its capture time, not current performance.

02

Look at balance and equity

Balance reflects realized results; equity also includes open profit and loss. Balance alone can hide floating losses. Drawdowns need a defined basis and sampling frequency.

03

Retain sources and methodology

Cash flows, fees, leverage and versions affect comparability. For third-party records, check verification scope and update times; a link is not proof that every metric has been validated.

This is a general guide to strategy evaluation and operations, not individualized investment advice.
